raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage as a function of the co-occurrence number for different methods. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 40% to 65%. The plot includes six lines, each representing a different method: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with pentagon markers), IKE (red line with inverted triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The Base method shows a relatively flat trend, maintaining an accuracy just above 40%. MEND and MEMIT show a moderate increase in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with MEMIT reaching the highest accuracy of around 60%. FT and IKE show a slight increase in accuracy, with FT reaching just below 50% and IKE just above 45%. ROME shows the most significant increase, starting just above 40% and reaching the highest accuracy of around 65%.
